newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China steps up HK border controls ahead of '97.
newsitem.headline: China steps up HK border controls ahead of '97.

text.p: Chinese authorities are clamping down on people attempting to sneak into Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's return to China next year, China's official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

Border guards have stepped up patrols near the frontier between southern China's Guangdong province and Hong Kong and since mid-1995 the province has conducted 13 drills to fight against illegal emigration, the agency said.
In the first three months of the year, Guangdong's frontier guards cracked 126 cases of illegal emigration, Xinhua said.
Meanwhile, about 12,000 Chinese who illegally crossed into the territory have been returned to the mainland this year, it said.

Zhang Shengqin, deputy-director of the Guangdong Public Security Department, was quoted as saying the measure will help boost the confidence of Hong Kong residents and maintain the territory's stability and prosperity.
Some ringleaders had fabricated rumours that the period before 1997 was the last opportunity to settle in Hong Kong, the news agency quoted Zhang as saying.
On Tuesday, the province mounted a large-scale security drill aimed at preventing a sudden storming of the border by Chinese citizens after the British colony is handed over to China.
